newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr sharply up in Tokyo, hits 34-mth high vs mark.
newsitem.headline: Dlr sharply up in Tokyo, hits 34-mth high vs mark.

text.p: The dollar gained fresh ground in Tokyo on Wednesday, rising as high as around 124.48 yen and hitting a fresh 34-month high of around 1.6892 marks.

The dollar's bullish trend against the mark overnight and a New York Times report on Wednesday saying that the number of U.S. companies expressing concern about the rise of the dollar has been surprisingly small lifted the dollar against the yen.
The New York Times report said that in recent days officials at Boeing Co, General Electric Co and Intel Corp had dismissed worries about the dollar.
"We can export our machines to Japan and Europe with a landed cost that is competitive, even at the current exchange rates," Gleason Corp Chairman James Gleason told the paper.

This report made traders in Tokyo comfortable about taking up fresh dollar positions in afternoon trade because they had been worried that rising complaints by U.S. exporters about the dollar's rise could be translated into a currency policy by the U.S. government, dealers said.
The dollar's performance against the mark stood out in morning trade, with an aggressive buying spree sparked mainly by a carry over of dollar-bullish sentiment overnight.

Overnight the greenback surged to a 33-month high on concerns about German economic problems and a report on Market News Services Inc, which quoted an unnamed source familiar with German finance officials as saying they would welcome a dollar rally to 1.70 to 1.75 marks.
"A fresh dollar bull trend has started. The market wants to see whether G7 statement will be backed up with actions," said a senior trader at a European bank in Tokyo.
The weekend's G7 meeting indicated a desire for currency stability and said the dollar has surged enough. This temporarily pushed the dollar close to 120 yen on Monday.
"The dollar is definitely breaking higher. If dollar/mark breaks the next key level of 1.69, we would see 1.70 very soon," said a local bank dealer in Singapore.
"The dollar/yen, once it hits 125, will come off by 200-300 points before it goes back up again," he said.
Some dealers in Tokyo said the Bank of Japan was likely to sell dollars for yen if the dollar appeared set to stride above the key 125-yen level, but others were uncertain.

Dealers in Tokyo said some Japanese investors and securities houses were active buyers. Purchases by securities houses were related to fresh dual samurai bond issues expected within this month, they said.

There was also talk that a major Japanese public fund had been buying U.S. Treasury bills and dollars since the G7 meeting. Dealers said the public fund had apparently been buying dollars and Treasury notes and bills for a long time and was one of driving forces behind the dollar's rise against the yen.
